parsed.use_case: Real-time monitoring services must track the exact 50th percentile of request latencies as continuous streams of RPC calls complete. Each incoming measurement must update the central metric immediately without re-ordering or rescanning the entire history of observed values.
system_examples: Biomedical sensor telemetry systems — computing the running median of continuous physiological readings to filter out impulse noise and motion artifacts as sensor samples arrive.
Algorithmic trade execution routers — maintaining the live median execution latency across exchange fills to dynamically adjust order routing thresholds without reprocessing past transactions.
parsed.explanation: The standard solution balances two heaps—a max-heap for the lower half of numbers and a min-heap for the upper half—yielding O(log N) insertions and O(1) median queries instead of the naive O(N log N) re-sorting or O(N) linear insertion. In production, however, maintaining an exact median over an unbounded stream is primarily a conceptual interview exercise because storing all historical elements consumes linear memory; industry telemetry systems instead deploy bounded-memory quantile sketches such as T-Digest or DDSketch.
